transcript.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Hamilton University. I'm Ms Roberts, one of the student advisers, and in the next few minutes I'd like to tell you about the events in your first week and about some useful services.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: I know that you probably have a lot of questions, and some of you may be feeling a little nervous. That is completely normal. Every student in this room felt the same on their first day, and by the end of the week you will be surprised how quickly you feel at home.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: First, the events. I know the first days can feel strange, so we organise something every day to help you meet people. The library tour was planned for Monday, but it has moved to Tuesday at ten o'clock.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: On Wednesday afternoon there is a sports taster session in the gym. You can try basketball, badminton or table tennis, and you don't need special clothes, only comfortable shoes.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: Thursday is the language café. It's held in the student common room, and it's a good chance to practise English with local students while you drink tea or coffee.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: On Friday evening we show a film in the main hall. This week it's an old comedy, and the tickets are free. I should add that the careers talk, which some of you asked about, is on Monday, in the first week, at two o'clock.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: All of these events are free, and you don't have to attend every one. Choose the ones that interest you most, and if you're feeling tired after your journey, it's perfectly acceptable to stay in your room and rest.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: Now some practical information. You must collect your student card from the Hamilton Building. That's H-A-M-I-L-T-O-N. You can't borrow books or enter the library without it, so please do it before the end of this week.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: If you lose your card, don't worry. A new one costs fifteen pounds. Last year it was twenty, but the university has reduced the price, so you will only pay fifteen.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: For the internet, you can connect to the university wifi everywhere on campus. You log in with your student number, and your password is the same one you use for email.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: If you have personal problems, or you feel homesick or stressed, our counselling service is here to help. It's free and confidential, and the office is on the second floor of the library building, next to the lifts.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: Many students say they were hesitant to ask for support at first, but then wished they had done it sooner. The advisers are not there to judge anyone, and everything you tell us is private.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: Finally, security. The security desk is open twenty-four hours a day, so if you ever feel unsafe at night, you can go there or call from any of the emergency phones. The number is printed on the back of your card.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: I would also recommend saving that number in your phone straight away. It costs nothing, and it could be very useful one day, for you or for a friend.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS

transcript.text: That's everything from me. Please pick up a booklet on your way out, and enjoy your first week.
transcript.speaker: MS ROBERTS
